newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mexico repayment of US loan not sign crisis over.
newsitem.headline: Mexico repayment of US loan not sign crisis over.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said on Friday that the country's paying back early of a $3.5 billion debt to the U.S. should not be seen as a sign the economic crisis was completely over.
"Some (people) have interpreted the pre-payment as meaning the crisis is over. But it was just a step," he told a news conference at the World Economic Forum.
Mexico announced on January 15 that it was paying the $3.5 billion outstanding on a February 1995 loan made by the U.S. Treasury at the height of the peso crisis.

Ortiz said that the country would only have fully recovered from its 1995 crisis, triggered by a massive devaluation of the Mexican currency, when living standards had recovered to their pre-crisis levels.
He said that the economy had recovered around 80 percent of the output lost in the 1995 crash when the economy slumped over six percent.
By the end of 1997, industrial output would be above pre-1995 levels but living standards would continue to lag, he said.
